value.body: A data scientist uses statistics and machine learning on data to answer business questions and build prediction models. Employers include product companies, banks, e-commerce, analytics and consulting firms, and startups. A typical day involves exploring data, building and testing models in Python, and explaining results to business teams.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech, B.Sc Statistics/Mathematics or MCA; many have a master's

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Python, SQL, scikit-learn, Jupyter, cloud ML platforms

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Direct fresher entry is limited; many start as data analysts or ML interns and move up. A strong portfolio of projects, statistics fundamentals and SQL help; a master's is common for research-heavy teams.

value.title: At a glance
items: Titles vary; some "data scientist" roles are mostly analytics.
Next roles: senior data scientist, ML engineer, analytics lead.
Generative AI tools are changing parts of the work.
